title: Tracing obscured galaxy build-up at high redshift using deep radio surveys
question: Explore the morphological and physical properties of high-redshift (z > 3) far-IR and radio-selected galaxies and investigate the interplay of star formation rate and supermassive black hole activity, particularly in merging systems.

what.value: 1.4 GHz VLA radio catalogues for COSMOS and ECDF-S

evidence.quote: Radio data were obtained from both fields at 1.4 GHz with the VLA (cite: 2010ApJS..188..384S; smolcic17; 2013ApJS..205...13M) at an angular resolution of $\sim 2.5''$.
The far-IR wavelength regime, which is necessary for our selection, is available through the Herschel Multi-tiered Extragalactic Survey (cite: hermes).

what.value: Cosmos2015 photometric catalogue fluxes and redshifts

evidence.quote: For this exploration, we consulted Simbad (cite: 2000A&AS..143....9W), the NED online search tools, and the Cosmos2015 (cite: Laigle16) online catalogue, retrieving redshift values from sources that are within 2 arcsec of our candidates.
The data fluxes from the Cosmos2015 catalogue were used in the analysis, while the radio information as well as any nebular emission component were not taken into consideration.

what.value: Cosmos2020 and HELP catalogues for photometric redshift and SED property comparisons

evidence.loc: Comparison of the retrieved z with photometric catalogues
evidence.quote: In more detail, the catalogues consist of the Cosmos2015 (cite: Laigle16), the Cosmos2020 (cite: 2022ApJS..258...11W) and the HELP catalogues (cite: 2021MNRAS.507..129S).

what.value: ALMA Band 3 spectroscopic redshifts for CVLA958 and ALESS33

evidence.quote: The recent work by (cite: 2021MNRAS.501.3926B) also identified the emission line as due to the CO4-3 rotational transition at band 3 of ALMA, locating this source at $z=3.1755$.

recipe.goal: Cross-match radio and far-IR catalogues and select high-z candidates
recipe.method: Cross-match VLA 1.4 GHz and HerMES catalogues within 18 arcsec, filter for S/N > 5, compact single radio sources (< 10 arcsec), 250/350/500 um flux errors < 50%, f_350um/f_250um > 1, and z > 3 from literature.
key_parameters: maximum separation = 18 arcsec, radio S/N > 5, angular size < 10 arcsec, far-IR flux errors < 50%, f_350um/f_250um > 1, redshift match radius = 2 arcsec

recipe.goal: Extract mm spectra from IRAM 30m and ALMA observations to determine spectroscopic redshifts
recipe.method: Scan 3 mm and 2 mm bands with IRAM 30m (removing outliers and correcting platforming) and extract ALMA Band 3 and Band 4 spectra using CASA to identify CO emission lines.
key_parameters: Gaussian filter of 50 km/s and redshift step of 0.01 (for IRAM spectrum search)

recipe.goal: Perform multi-wavelength SED fitting to derive physical properties and AGN fractions
recipe.method: Fit multi-wavelength photometry (excluding radio and nebular emission) using CIGALE to obtain best-fit and Bayesian estimates of stellar mass, SFR_IR, L_IR, AGN fraction, and photometric redshift.
key_parameters: sfhdelayed, bc03 (Chabrier IMF), dustatt_2powerlaws, lyc_absorption, dl2014, fritz2006 AGN model, delta_z = 0.1 for photo-z fitting
assumptions: Chabrier IMF; cosmology H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7

recipe.goal: Calculate radio luminosities, radio-based SFRs, and q_TIR to assess AGN radio excess
recipe.method: Compute L_1.4GHz, derive SFR_radio using Bell (2003) equation 6 assuming radio emission is purely from star formation, and compute q_TIR from L_IR (42-122 um) and L_1.4GHz.
assumptions: Radio spectral index alpha = 0.8 for pure radio synchrotron emission
